utterances.text: Sadness.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Witness, it is clear from your evidence that you had known Dusko Tadic for a number of years. Can you tell the Court anything about his character?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A good friend, a good father, a good parent, a good husband. There is nothing which is not good I can tell you about him, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: When did you last see Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they were supposed to leave for Germany.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Can you remember when that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was sometime around August or September, just before the start of the school year in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: That is all I ask.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Your Honour, perhaps I could make the same request that Miss de Bertodano made and have the sound turned off for a moment because I will be asking questions that would otherwise transgress the purpose of the facial distortion?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. That may be done. You just let the technical people know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK. If we can have the sound turned off now? 26 27 28

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Nothing arising, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to this witness being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Witness, you are free to leave at this time and go home. However, you are subject to being recalled for testimony before the Tribunal, so you should make yourself available. Keep in touch with Miss de Bertodano and if she tells you that you have been asked to return, then you should return. Will you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for coming. You should remain in your seat and then we will leave for five minutes -- is that enough -- and then we will return.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, would you call your next witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We call Mira Tadic. MIRA TADIC, called

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would you please take the oath that has been handed to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated Mr. Kay, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is your name Mira Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you the wife of Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us when you were married to Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 2nd August 1979.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts did that marriage take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not get married straightaway. First, we went to the seaside and then we got married later on in Kozarac after a year.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The marriage in Kozarac, did that take place in a church or a public building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the local office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you have children by your marriage to Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, two daughters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What are their names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The older one is called Valentina and the younger one Alexandra.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you come from the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born in the village of Vidovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could look at the Defence Exhibit 13A so that we can see that on the map? If you could just look at that map for a moment, madam, just to familiarise yourself with it and then we will put it on the screen beside you. Do you see Kozarac in the middle of the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you see the village of Vidovici on the right-hand side of the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps at this stage for information purposes that could just be put on the overhead projector? Thank you. The village of Vidovici there is on the outskirts of Kozarac, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, three kilometres away from Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What is your maiden name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Does your family originate and is your family centred in that area of Vidovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do your parents still live there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do other close relatives of yours still live in that village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some do, some do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts do you live now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that with your two children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What is your job?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am a nurse.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where do you work as a nurse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the local clinic in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you qualify to or train to become a nurse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did you finish your training?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In 1979, in May 1979.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you been largely employed as a nurse since 1979?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You are working at present in the hospital in Prijedor. Have you worked in other hospitals in opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, only at the hospital in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am going to ask you some questions now about your background. When did you first start to live with Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since August 1979.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how long had you known him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I met him in January 1976.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had you seen him in Kozarac, did you know about him in Kozarac before you first met him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew about him, but I did not know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you attend school in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you could tell us how old you are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to school in Kozarac up until I was 15 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And how old are you now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Had you had any connection with the Tadic family before you met Dusko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Having met Dusko Tadic in 1976, did you get to know other members of his family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not during that year, but later on, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So did you get to know his father Ostoja?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: His mother Staka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And his brothers Ljubo, Stojan and Mladen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did the Tadic family know your family? For instance, did Ostoja Tadic know your father?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What is the name of your father?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Radovan Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Growing up as you did in Kozarac, how would you describe the relations between the different ethnic communities that we know existed in that town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I grew up in Kozarac and the relationship between the nationalities was very good. We went to school together. We would help one another. Everything was well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How would you describe your ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am a Serb from Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you have Muslim friends and Croat friends who lived in the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you came to know Dusko Tadic did he have Muslim friends and Croat friends in the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have put the time of your marrying Dusko Tadic as being 1979 when you went on holiday together. Is that because you started living together as a couple?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us what work Dusko Tadic was doing at that time? What was his job?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time when we got married we were both unemployed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did Dusko Tadic later on become employed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a year later, somewhere in October 1980.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What sort of work did he do then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then he worked in Banja Luka at the Rudi Cajavec company.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What is the work of that company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was a military, a military part of that company. They were making some electronic appliances.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As far as you knew, did Dusko Tadic then have work as an electrician or as an electrical engineer in that factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know how to describe it. He was connecting some parts, I do not know for what purpose, but anyway he had secondary school type of qualifications.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how long did he work there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He worked there up until 1986.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did you first get your job as a nurse having qualified in 1979?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 15th October 1979.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us the year when you had your first child?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 11th April 1980.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did Dusko Tadic always remain in employment or did he ever have periods when he was unemployed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He started to work in October 1980. Until 1986 he worked in the Cajavec company.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Sorry, I did not understand that. In what company? If you could repeat your last answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since October 1979 up until the beginning of 1986 he worked in Banja Luka at the Rudi Cajavec company.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: After that time of 1986 was he ever unemployed or has he always been continuously in employment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that period in 1986 I went to Libya. Then he stopped working and went there with me, and when we came back in 1987 he opened a private company for some construction work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it you then who first of all got a job in Libya?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was that work in Libya?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I worked as a nurse.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did Dusko Tadic go to Libya with you or did he travel to Libya separately and at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He came later after me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you ever been divorced from Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly the year, probably 1987, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that when you came back from Libya or whilst you were in Libya?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when we came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you take your eldest daughter to Libya with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, my husband brought her with him when he arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how long did you work in Libya?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Up until the end of 1986, from January till November 1986.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you lived in Libya did Dusko Tadic get a job?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, officially he was working in his firm, in his company in Banja Luka, but he asked for a break in order to be able to accompany me. So officially he was employed but he was not working.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Before you left for Libya did the two of you spend your early married life in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in Kozarac in the family house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that the house where the family still live today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could look at a photograph now just to identify that. Prosecution Exhibit 300, I think it is 300A and B or Prosecution Exhibit 300. If you could just look at that for a moment and then if it could be put on the projector so that people can see it. (Handed). Is that the house that you spoke of that we see in the photograph on the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is that house but without that extended part of it. That is what it looked like when we went to Libya.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The picture we see now is a house that has been extended since the early days of your marriage, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As we look at that photograph now, can you indicate to us by turning to your right and pointing with the steel pointer the part of the building where you lived in the early years of your marriage before 1986?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated on the photograph] That is the part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is it right that today that is now in fact a cafe and bar run by Dusko Tadic's brother Mladen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. When you came back from Libya at the end of 1986, whereabouts did the two of you then go and live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the end of 1986 we came back but in early 1987, that is in the spring of 1987, we moved into private accommodation in Kalate, in the Rade Kondic Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is another different part of Kozarac from where the family home is situated, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this is a small street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, but it is in a different street from where the family home is situated in Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is a different street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What sort of accommodation did you have there in 1987?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had the whole, the entire ground floor of the house. It was good accommodation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was the cause for your divorce in 1987?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In 1987 Dule and I tried to go to a foreign country as a nurse. There was a possibility to get a job in Switzerland, but there was a high chance, a high probability to get a job if one was single. That is why we divorced.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So would it be right to describe it as a divorce of convenience?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, by common accord.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you get that job in Switzerland that you hoped to get as a single nurse?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did the divorce get processed through the authorities in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, officially we divorced in court by mutual agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you ever remarry or get undivorced?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But did you and he continue living together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We have always lived together.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The youngest child that you have, what is the date of birth of that child?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 3rd March 1989.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In 1987 did Dusko Tadic, having returned from Libya, find other work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in 1987 he created his own company.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember the name of that company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were doing carpentry work for construction buildings. That is how it was called then. It was in Sisak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where is Sisak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where was the company based?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Sisak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did he go to work in Croatia for the company that he had formed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The company was not doing actually work where it was founded, but on various construction sites in Zagreb, Ljubljana, Belgrade, wherever they agreed to do a particular job.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did he form that company on his own or was anyone else involved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With a colleague, not on his own.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was that colleague's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fikret Salkanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Working for that company did they employ other people to work with them or was it just the two of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They employed other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At this time did you return to work as a nurse when you had come back from Libya?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, was that in the hospital in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I made a mistake. Since 1992 I worked in the hospital in Prijedor, and up until '92 I worked at the hospital in Kozarac. This is basically the same company, but there were two various places where I worked. Basically I lived and worked in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So when you said that your first job as a nurse was later on in 1979, was that working at the hospital in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I made a mistake initially.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that hospital in fact run by the major hospital in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We thought that we would talk with counsel for a few moments. So, Mrs. Tadic, you are free to leave. You should return tomorrow at 10 a.m., please. We are going to remain here a moment to talk with the attorneys. So you are free to leave now. (The witness withdrew).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We thought that we would use this new mechanism of turning off the sound, so I would like to ask the technician to turn off the sound that will enable us to talk confidentially with counsel. 26 27 28

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: (The court adjourned until the following day). 28
